examples.scenario: A parcel polygon self-intersects but still loads successfully.
examples.reason: Successful parsing does not imply OGC/GEOS validity; invalid geometry can produce incorrect spatial results.

examples.scenario: A polygon ring is not closed but rasterization still returns pixels.
examples.reason: Canonical parcel membership must fail closed before rasterization when polygon validity is not proven.

examples.scenario: MakeValid converts one Polygon into a MultiPolygon.
examples.reason: Repair can change topology and geometry type; the result is derived and cannot silently replace the authoritative parcel.

examples.scenario: MakeValid returns a GeometryCollection containing polygon and line components.
examples.reason: Lower-dimensional repair artifacts can affect downstream interpretation and must be explicitly removed or reviewed.

examples.scenario: A repaired boundary loses area compared with the original invalid shape.
examples.reason: Repair ambiguity means area and topology differences must be captured before any raster membership is accepted.

examples.scenario: The target parcel is individually valid but overlaps an adjacent parcel.
examples.reason: Individual validity does not prove a consistent parcel coverage; overlapping interiors are a coverage error.

examples.scenario: Two adjacent parcels appear to share an edge but vertex segmentation differs.
examples.reason: Coverage validity requires matching shared boundary segments.

examples.scenario: A narrow sliver gap exists between neighboring parcels.
examples.reason: Gap detection is allowed, but automatically moving authoritative boundaries is not.

examples.scenario: Coverage cleaning is used automatically to remove a gap before sampling.
examples.reason: Cleaning creates a derived coverage and cannot silently redefine the parcel.

examples.scenario: Default rasterization and ALL_TOUCHED select different edge pixels.
examples.reason: Membership mode must be defined and serialized rather than selected after seeing extrema.

examples.scenario: ALL_TOUCHED is enabled and two parcel polygons touch at a pixel edge.
examples.reason: GDAL documents that feature order can determine the burned edge pixel.

examples.scenario: Feature order changes between two ALL_TOUCHED replays.
examples.reason: Reproducible membership requires stable ordering or a mode that avoids order-dependent ambiguity.

examples.scenario: A polygon boundary only touches a pixel center.
examples.reason: GDAL documents unspecified behavior for the exact center-touch case; the project must define an explicit tie policy.

examples.scenario: Parcel membership is computed before CRS transformation is verified.
examples.reason: Pixel addressing is invalid until boundary and raster are proven in the same coordinate space.

examples.scenario: One vertex fails transformation but the remaining vertices form a polygon.
examples.reason: Every boundary vertex must transform successfully before membership can be trusted.

examples.scenario: A repaired geometry is treated as canonical because its vertex count is similar.
examples.reason: Similarity does not prove authoritative equivalence; type, parts, area, topology and digest must be compared.

examples.scenario: Ring orientation differs between two equivalent polygon files.
examples.reason: GEOS does not enforce a particular ring orientation for validity, so orientation alone is not a valid rejection rule.

examples.scenario: A 3D MultiPolygon is valid in Z-separated space but overlaps in XY.
examples.reason: GEOS validity is two-dimensional; raster membership is also driven by planar geometry.

examples.scenario: Rasterization is repeated twice and returns different pixel sets.
examples.reason: The exact ordered pixel-index set must replay identically before extrema sampling.

examples.scenario: Only the count of selected pixels matches between two runs.
examples.reason: Equal counts do not prove the same cells were selected.

examples.scenario: A parcel contains an interior hole but pixels in the hole are included.
examples.reason: Interior rings define excluded regions and must remain excluded from parcel membership.

examples.scenario: A multipart parcel has one component outside the downloaded raster extent.
examples.reason: All parcel components must be covered before extrema are final.

examples.scenario: The selected parcel intersects only masked/nodata raster cells.
examples.reason: Empty valid-pixel membership is a data condition, not permission to invent elevation.

examples.scenario: A single-pixel parcel is rejected merely because the membership count is one.
examples.reason: A one-cell result can be legitimate when geometry, transform, pixel semantics and validity are all proven.

examples.scenario: Rasterization uses a new GDAL version and selected edge pixels change.
examples.reason: Version/runtime changes must be captured and deterministic output compared.

examples.scenario: The parcel boundary serializes differently after format round-trip but topology is unchanged.
examples.reason: Byte differences alone may be formatting; semantic geometry must also be reconciled.

examples.scenario: Static geometry QA completes while canonical point rows remain zero.
examples.reason: Boundary and membership guards can advance without fabricating target coordinates.

examples.scenario: The runner ACK is absent, so a second rasterization runner is started.
examples.reason: The continuation contract requires the existing single shared runner.

examples.scenario: Known execution blockers are shown as pending to make the dashboard appear active.
examples.reason: Known unresolved conditions stay blocked; pending remains zero.

examples.scenario: The geometry-membership package is reported as final height-difference accuracy.
examples.reason: Real height difference still requires canonical points, authoritative boundary binding, immutable raster execution, numeric sampling and readback.
